Maria B.: heads-up — we're seeing a spike in pod evictions on gpu-nodes in eu-west-1, kubelet is marking network unhealthy and evicting pods
Ashwin R.: ugh. Are these full node NotReady events or just network conditions reported by the kubelet health probe?
Maria B.: kubelet logs show: "network probe failed: dial tcp <10.x.x.x>:10250: i/o timeout" repeatedly for ~30s then eviction starts
k8s-alert-bot: [Alert] node/gpu-node-032: KubeletNetworkReadinessFailure (threshold exceeded)
kevin.l: any recent kernel or NIC driver rollouts in that AZ? RDMA/GPUDirect changes?
we had a driver update last week on the dedicated pool
Maria B.: driver update rolled out 2 days ago to take advantage of GPUDirect. Rollout was staged but only this AZ shows high east-west packet loss in perf metrics
julia_ops: could be MTU mismatch + overlay (calico) + RDMA causing fragmentation/reordering. We've seen kubelet probes fail if packets are dropped under small bursts.
Ashwin R.: let's gather quick signals: iperf between nodes, mtr to the node IPs, kernel drop counters, and `ethtool -k` to check offloads
Maria B.: running quick checks now. iperf shows intermittent throughput dips, `dmesg` on node has some NIC tx timeouts. `ethtool -S` shows increases in tx_queue_drops.
Also seeing lots of TCP retransmits on `ss -s`.
kevin.l: can you dump a kubelet log snippet? curious which probe is failing (read-only /healthz or the network plugin webhook?)
Maria B.: snippet:
```
Mar 10 14:03:12 gpu-node-032 kubelet[1234]: I0310 14:03:12.123456   1234 kuberuntime_manager.go:xxxx] NetworkReady check failed: dial tcp 10.244.3.1:4194: i/o timeout
Mar 10 14:03:42 gpu-node-032 kubelet[1234]: I0310 14:03:42.654321   1234 eviction_manager.go:yyy] attempt to reclaim resources
Mar 10 14:03:43 gpu-node-032 kubelet[1234]: I0310 14:03:43.654333   1234 eviction_manager.go:zzz] Evicting pod default/model-serve-abcde
```
Ashwin R.: that `10.244.*` address is calico ipip tunnel on that node overlay, so traffic between pods on different nodes is hitting the IP-in-IP path
julia_ops: if ipip MTU is too big for NIC+RDMA path we can get fragmentation or drops. Check `ip link` MTU on host vs. the calico_mtu (felix) setting
also check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_retries1` causing early timeouts
kevin.l: short-term mitigation: increase kubelet's `--pod-eviction-timeout` and node-monitor-grace to avoid evictions from short blips. Long-term: fix underlying drops
Maria B.: proposed kubelet flags to test on a single node (will follow canary):
```
--pod-eviction-timeout=8m0s  # from 1m to 8m
--node-monitor-grace=3m     # from 40s to 3m
--node-status-update-frequency=20s
```
Ashwin R.: +1 for canary. Also enable debug `tcpdump -i <iface> -w /tmp/nettrace.pcap` for the problematic time window so we can inspect fragmentation/ICMP messages
julia_ops: we should also try disabling offloads (gso/tso/gro) temporarily on one host to see if it reduces reordering: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`
that often surfaces with RDMA drivers
kevin.l: if it's calico ipip, consider switching that pool to VXLAN or use direct routing (no encapsulation) for nodes in the same AZ. VXLAN has a slightly different fragmentation profile
Maria B.: created a canary rollout: changed kubelet flags on gpu-node-032 and started tcpdump + iperf in loop. will report in 15m.
k8s-alert-bot: [Info] Created incident INC-20240310-58 for node-network-health-flap
Ashwin R.: if canary stabilizes, let's make a cluster-wide change: adjust Felix MTU or CNI config + coordinate RDMA driver vendor on-call to check firmware bug
Maria B.: update: after disabling GSO/TCP offload on the canary, the node stopped reporting network probe failures. iperf looks steady. no new evictions in 20m.
julia_ops: sounds like an offload/driver interaction. We'll schedule a vendor escalation and plan a staged fix (disable offloads on nodes with GPUDirect until driver patch available).
We should also submit a kubelet config change doc for increasing eviction timeouts so transient infra blips don't cause mass evictions.
kevin.l: agree. action items: 1) keep canary for 2h with offloads off and collect pcaps; 2) create PR to bump pod-eviction-timeout & node-monitor-grace in our kubelet DaemonSet for dedicated pools; 3) vendor escalation for NIC/RDMA driver
Maria B.: noted. I'll also add a Grafana panel showing calico tunnel drops + kubelet network probe failure rate to catch regressions earlier. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ashwin R.: thanks team. if anyone sees more evictions ping me and @julia_ops. We'll avoid mass restarts while this is under investigation :pray:
kevin.l: thumbs up :thumbsup:
